content_html:
WhatsApp message template examples you can adapt

These WhatsApp message template examples cover the messages most businesses need: welcome, order, appointment, payment, feedback, offers, win-back and one-time passcodes. Each example shows the category it belongs to and uses numbered variables such as {{1}} for details like the customer's name. Adapt the wording to your brand, add clear sample values when you submit, and you will have a strong starting library.

How to use these WhatsApp message template examples

  1. Pick the example closest to what you need.
  2. Change the wording to match how your brand speaks.
  3. Choose the right category: utility, marketing or authentication.
  4. Add realistic sample values for each variable when submitting.
  5. Add buttons where they help the customer act.

For how templates are structured and approved, see our WhatsApp template library guide.

Utility template examples

Order confirmation

"Hi {{1}}, thanks for your order {{2}}. We have received ₹{{3}} and will ship your items within 2 days. We will message you here when they are on the way." Button: Track order.

Shipping update

"Good news, {{1}}! Your order {{2}} has shipped with {{3}}. Expected delivery: {{4}}." Button: Track shipment.

Appointment reminder

"Hi {{1}}, this is a reminder of your appointment with {{2}} on {{3}} at {{4}}. Please arrive 10 minutes early." Buttons: Confirm, Reschedule.

Payment reminder

"Hi {{1}}, your payment of ₹{{2}} for {{3}} is due on {{4}}. Tap below to pay securely." Button: Pay now.

Feedback request

"Hi {{1}}, how was your experience with us today? Your feedback helps us improve." Buttons: Great, Okay, Not good.

Marketing template examples

Welcome message

"Welcome to {{1}}, {{2}}! You will now get early access to new arrivals and member-only offers here. Reply STOP anytime to opt out."

Festive offer

"Hi {{1}}, our festive sale is live! Enjoy {{2}}% off on selected styles until {{3}}." Button: Shop now.

Back in stock

"{{1}}, the {{2}} you liked is back in stock. Sizes are limited, so grab yours soon." Button: View product.

Win-back

"We miss you, {{1}}! It has been a while since your last visit. Here is a special code for your next order: {{2}}." Button: Copy code.

For more on offers, read our WhatsApp promotional messages guide.

Authentication template example

"{{1}} is your verification code. For your security, do not share this code." Button: Copy code. Authentication templates follow a fixed format set by Meta, so you mostly choose options rather than writing free text.

Tips for getting templates approved

  • Never start or end a message with a variable.
  • Give each variable enough text around it to make its meaning clear.
  • Keep utility templates free of offers, or they will be classed as marketing.
  • Avoid all-caps, too many emojis and vague text such as "Click here".
  • Do not ask for card numbers, PINs or passwords.

Meta's template guidelines list the current rules.

Languages

If your customers speak Hindi or another regional language, submit each template in that language too, under the same template name. Have a native speaker check the tone, because a literal translation can sound stiff.

Need templates written for you?

We write, submit and manage templates as part of our WhatsApp AI chatbot and automation service. You can also see how templates power cart recovery and other automations.

Frequently asked questions

Can I copy these templates as they are?

Use them as a starting point. Change the wording to match your brand and fill in clear sample values when you submit them.

How many variables can a template have?

Templates can carry several variables, but each one needs clear text around it. Too many variables in a short message can lead to rejection.

Can templates include buttons?

Yes. Templates can carry quick-reply buttons, a call button or a website link button.
